title: Entanglement Sudden Death: Eberly's Work and the Limits of Local Dynamics
abstract: Entanglement sudden death (ESD), explored through a series of works by Yu and Eberly, supports the notion of entanglement vanishing abruptly and completely at a finite time, even when the underlying open-system dynamics remain smooth. In this article, we revisit the development of ESD from bipartite origins to genuine multipartite entanglement. We first illustrate the canonical mechanism of ESD with two independently damped qubits, for which the concurrence vanishes at a finite time while populations and coherences remain nonzero. We next present our results on multipartite entanglement for generalized GHZ states under depolarization. Global and independent local depolarizing dynamics can be chosen to produce identical reduced evolution for every individual qubit, yet they yield different genuine-multipartite-entanglement sudden death times, whose ordering can reverse with the initial state. For N-qubit GHZ states, this distinction becomes asymptotically stronger since the ESD time scales as 1/N under independent local depolarization, whereas under global depolarization it approaches a finite value in the thermodynamic limit. Echoing a central lesson of Prof. Eberly's work, we report the lifetime of multipartite entanglement is not fixed by the local dynamics, but rather depends on the evolution of the joint quantum state.
summary: This paper explores Entanglement Sudden Death (ESD), demonstrating that the abrupt loss of entanglement in multipartite systems is highly sensitive to the noise model applied. By comparing global versus local depolarization on GHZ states, the authors prove that the entanglement lifetime depends on the joint evolution, not just the local dynamics. This highlights that understanding entanglement requires analyzing the entire composite system state.
main_problem: The paper investigates Entanglement Sudden Death (ESD), the phenomenon where entanglement vanishes abruptly at a finite time despite the underlying system dynamics remaining smooth.
main_result: The lifetime of genuine multipartite entanglement depends critically on the nature of the noise (global vs. local), showing that local dynamics alone do not determine the ESD time or its scaling with system size.
method: The authors analyze entanglement decay using measures like concurrence for both bipartite and multipartite systems, comparing dynamics under different noise models.
model_or_system: The study models open quantum systems, specifically using N-qubit GHZ states subjected to different types of environmental noise, such as independent local depolarization versus global depolarization.
key_observables: Concurrence, genuine multipartite entanglement, and the ESD time scale.
important_parameters: System size N, and the relative strength of local versus global noise coupling.
main_assumptions: The 'suddenness' refers only to the finite time of entanglement vanishing, not a sudden change in the density matrix evolution itself.
figures_summary: The notes reference figures comparing the ESD times for global versus independent local depolarization for N=3 qubits.
paper_structure: The paper revisits the concept of ESD from bipartite systems to genuine multipartite entanglement, first illustrating the mechanism with two qubits, and then comparing the ESD times for N-qubit GHZ states under global versus local depolarization.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to AMO physics and open quantum systems as it provides a rigorous, quantitative comparison of how different noise assumptions affect the fundamental persistence of quantum correlations in multi-particle systems.

The solid red line refers to dynamics under global depolarization and the dotted blue represents qubits subjected to independent depolarization. While independently depolarized states lose tripartite genuine entanglement faster than global white noise for this initial state, for sufficiently weakly entangled states, such as θ = π/128, have opposite order in which dynamics retains genuine correlations longer, as shown inset. (b) Entanglement sudden death time as a function amount of initial entanglement parametrized by the superposition angle θ in the initial GHZ state.
